tool_input.title: shop/api CrashLoopBackOff - wrong dnsConfig search domain
tool_input.content:
Incident: KubePodCrashLooping, namespace=shop, deployment=api, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab, kubeconfig-642bee834eb69ff0).

**Root cause:** Deployment api revision 2 added `dnsPolicy: None` + explicit `dnsConfig` with `searches: [shop.svc.cluster.internal, svc.cluster.internal, cluster.internal]` and nameserver 10.96.0.10. The cluster's actual domain (confirmed via `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system`, Corefile `kubernetes cluster.local ...`) is `cluster.local`, not `cluster.internal`. Because dnsPolicy was `None`, kubelet used ONLY the supplied (wrong) dnsConfig with no fallback — new pods could not resolve any in-cluster Service name (e.g. `redis`), got `[Errno -2] Name does not resolve`, and the app's startup code exits(1) after 5 failed redis connection attempts, causing CrashLoopBackOff.

This change was NOT present in the deployment's `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation — it was injected via a direct patch/edit outside the normal apply flow (worth asking "who/what patches this deployment post-apply" if it recurs).

**Why this is tricky:** Old ReplicaSet pods (previous revision, no dnsConfig override, dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst) kept running fine on the SAME node, serving 200s — so this looks like "the pod is just unhealthy" rather than a DNS-domain mismatch unless you diff the full pod spec (not just image/env) between old and new ReplicaSets.

**How to apply / diagnose fast next time:**
1. `kubectl get rs -n <ns>` — compare old vs new ReplicaSet pod templates line by line (not just image), especially `dnsPolicy`/`dnsConfig`.
2. `kubectl logs <crashing-pod> --previous` — look for "Name does not resolve" / getaddrinfo errors pointing to DNS.
3. `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml` — confirm the real cluster domain (usually `cluster.local`) and compare against any custom dnsConfig searches.
4. Fix: remove the dnsPolicy:None/dnsConfig override (revert to default ClusterFirst) or correct search domain to match coredns Corefile's authoritative zone. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>` is viable if a prior good revision exists.
5. Check `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` to confirm whether the bad pods are already excluded from traffic (readiness gating) — often this is a stuck/degraded rollout, not a full outage.
tool_input.description: On cluster aurora-lab, Deployment shop/api crash-looped because a rollout set dnsPolicy:None with dnsConfig.searches using 'cluster.internal' instead of the real cluster domain 'cluster.local', breaking DNS resolution of in-cluster Service names (e.g. redis) for new pods only.
